## TL;DR

The review identified two ways the requested last-activity time was missing or inaccurate: check-progress displays did not expose a recency tip, and Pipeline tips used the task update time rather than agent activity. I attached the shared tooltip data to those progress displays and changed Pipeline to receive the same activity timestamp the Board uses. Silent/stuck inline signals and the existing elapsed display remain intact. The focused card tests and required scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

I started from review pass 5, which named three concrete paths to address: the TaskCard check-progress rendering, the PipelineCard check-progress rendering, and the Pipeline timing source. I inspected the current branch’s task specification and component code, then followed the props from PipelineView into PipelineCard. PipelineView already had a `lastActivityFor(taskId)` helper backed by `repo.agentActivityAt` with `repo.runningSince` as the fallback. That made it possible to pass the activity timestamp into the Pipeline card without inventing a new timing rule.

For TaskCard, the compact check-progress component appears separately from the normal card hint. That explains why fixing only the hint builder could never make its recency visible. I wrapped the progress display in a focusable tooltip trigger with the same `data-tip` and touch behavior used elsewhere. For lifecycle hints classified as checks, I also included the activity tip so confirming-handoff and other check status labels can expose it. The coding status continues to show only its concise label in the line; the existing styled tooltip contains the last activity and explanatory text. Stuck and silent status decisions continue to use the shared status and evidence logic, so useful silence signals remain on the line.

For PipelineCard, the old tooltip described elapsed time since `stateSince`. That value is based on task updates and can predate recent agent output, matching the review’s concern. The card now formats the actual `lastActivityAt` prop with `agentLastActivityTip`, consistent with TaskCard. The step label remains the tooltip trigger for a normal status row, and the check-progress component receives the same tooltip attributes when it replaces that row. The elapsed text still appears for states that use it inline, including stuck cards.

I added coverage to the existing #1058 component test file for both progress paths and revised Pipeline assertions to distinguish last activity from the older state-start timestamp. I also supplied PipelineCard’s new prop in its shared test factory. During the first focused run, the check-progress test failed because its fake TaskCheckRun omitted `output`, which the production card parser reads. I replaced that abbreviated object with a complete minimal run payload; the focused card tests then passed.

## Approaches tried

I first compared the component props and rendering branches called out in the review. The key decision was to propagate agent activity rather than reformat `stateSince`, because the latter represents a different event. I then placed the tooltip on the actual check-progress trigger instead of creating a parallel popover implementation. This reuses the site’s delegated styled tooltip behavior, including keyboard focus and touch activation, while preserving each progress component’s own layout and content.

I ran the targeted component tests during development. The first run exposed the incomplete test fixture described above. After correcting it, all eight tests in the #1058 activity file passed. I then ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` as required. Its first remote validation run built successfully but reported the same fixture issue across the full changed-path suite; the runner automatically retried on another host after a hang, and the malformed test was then fixed. The subsequent required run passed the remote build and changed-path tests, plus local format, lint, build staleness, CSS layering, theme contrast, hard-coded color scan, rendered contrast, bare-require scan, task-asset guard, and UI smoke checks.

## Challenges and blockers

Remote validation hung once on the first host and retried on an alternate host. The first complete test pass correctly failed because the added test data was not shaped like a real TaskCheckRun. No production bug was found in that path after the fixture was corrected. The successful gate completed after the second runner retry; no human or device-only verification was needed for these criteria.

## Key learnings

The Board and Pipeline can share the same semantic meaning for last activity while still rendering it through different status components. The timestamp must come from agent activity state, not from the task’s update timestamp or the time a Pipeline state began. Also, when a status is rendered through a separate progress component, its tooltip must be attached at that component’s actual trigger; changes to the sibling hint line do not cover it. Finally, test doubles for active check runs need the stable fields consumed by all card-derived evidence helpers, even when a given assertion only cares about `running`.
